hints: Look carefully at the two curves X and Y. Which one has the higher hump and which one has the lower hump, and what does that tell you about needing energy to get started?
Remember enzymes lower activation energy but do not change start and end levels. Check what W connects (peak to peak) and what Z connects (substrate level to product level).
walkthrough:
**Compare the two curves**

Look at the key. X is the dotted line with the tall peak. Y is the dashed line with the short peak.

Both start at the same substrate energy and end at the same product energy. Only the height of the hump is different.

**Recall what enzymes do**

Enzymes speed up reactions by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy.

Activation energy is the energy needed to go from substrate level up to the top of the hump. So the lower hump, Y, must be the reaction with the enzyme.

**Identify W and Z**

W is the vertical arrow between the two peaks. It is not a full activation energy, it is the amount saved, the difference in activation energy.

Z is the vertical arrow from substrate level down to product level. That is the overall energy change (energy released), which is the same with or without enzyme.

options.A: X is indeed without the enzyme because it has the higher peak, but W is not the full activation energy, it is only the difference between the two peaks.
options.B: X has the higher peak so it is without the enzyme, not with. Z is correctly the overall energy change, but the first part is wrong.
options.C: Y has the lower peak so it is with the enzyme, and W between the peaks correctly shows how much the activation energy is lowered.
options.D: Z is the overall energy change (energy lost from substrate to product), not energy gained, and W is the difference, not the full activation energy with enzyme.
